newsitem.title: UK: Cricket-England draw first blood, but Taylor stays calm.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-England draw first blood, but Taylor stays calm.

text.p: Australia's reputation as world champions was shattered by a resurgent England on Sunday, but captain Mark Taylor insisted it was not time to panic despite losing the first test at Edgbaston by nine wickets.
Taylor admitted his team, who have beaten West Indies and South Africa in the past year, were outplayed but insisted their poor performance should not provoke major team changes.
"It's not time to panic or make wholesale changes," said Taylor, who was dismissed for 129 early in the day after a wretched run of form with the bat.
"I'm obviously relieved to have made runs myself, but I'd prefer to make nought and win the game."

Winning was never a real possibility once Australia were bowled out in difficult conditions for 118 on the first day and after showing signs of a fightback, the tourists surrendered with a day to spare.
England, who surrendered the Ashes to Australia in 1989, won the one-day series 3-0 and their convincing win inside four days will give them a huge psychological boost in the six-test series.
With the weather always uncertain, their hopes of salvaging a draw rose on Sunday as centuries by Taylor and Greg Blewett (125) carried them to 393 for three at one stage.
But the tourists' middle-order badly let them down, capitulating on a tame batting strip in much the same vein as they did in the first innings.
Australia lost their last their last seven wickets for just 84 runs, handing England victory on a silver plate.

Mike Atherton, widely criticised in recent years for his team's lame performances, feasted on the opportunity hammering a quickfire 57 to guide England to the victory target of 118 in just 21.3 overs.
Australia needed a big contribution from Mark Waugh, who had been discharged from hospital before play began after suffering from a virus, and his twin Steve.
Gough was brought back to dismiss both, however, and Mark Ealham wrapped up the innings with three wickets for nought in the space of 10 balls.
England lost Mark Butcher for 14 with the total on 29, but with rain forecast for Monday, Atherton and Alec Stewart (39 not out) made sure of the win before the day was out.
If Taylor's return to form with his first test century in three years was the most positive aspect of the match for Australia, Warne's lack of success was the most worrying.
He will need to live up to his reputation as the world's best spin bowler if Australia are to reverse the trend in which the team winning the first Ashes test takes the series.
The second test begins at Lord's on June 19.
